newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 2.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 2.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Monday:

* On Friday, the Dow Jones industrial average closed up 0.86 points to 7,331.04, reversing a sell-off that pushed the blue chip index down as much as 88 points in early trading. The Dow index fell 14.87 points for the week.

* Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Monday that the government had indicated that deregulation of the manufacturing sector, which was scheduled this month, would focus on the reduction of import duty.

* On Sunday, Indonesia's ruling Golkar party said that the high voter turnout and its record victory in last week's election legitimised the existing government despite the most violent political violence ever.

* Indonesia's military on Sunday blamed the deaths of 17 security force members in a separatist ambush in East Timor on an operational mistake that left the returning election security unit vunerable to attack.
MARKET
* On Friday, Jakarta stocks ended up but off highs in a continuing wave of optimism following last week's general election, brokers said. The index closed 0.95 percent higher at 696.03 points.
* On Monday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,430.50/31.50 at 0125 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,431.50/32.00.
STOCKS TO WATCH
* Heavyweight telecommunications firm PT Telkom after announcement last Friday of its first quarter results and future plans.

* The country's largest noodle maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur following its encouraging net profit in the first quarter of 1997, and on Monday's announcement that it plans to raise its paid-up capital.
* Prasidha Aneka Niaga following a significant increase in coffee prices
* Property firm PT Surya Semesta Internusa on market talk of higher-than-expected net profit in the first quarter and also its shareholders' meeting on June 15.
* Cable maker GT Kabel Indonesia ahead its extraordinary shareholders' meeting on June 25, which will discuss its proposed stock split.
* Report in Bisnis Indonesia on Monday said Saudi Arabia had imposed a fee for imported tyres to receive local certification, which could dampen sentiment on tyre-maker Gadjah Tunggal.
* Toll road operator Citra Marga said on Monday it will hold a shareholders' meeting on June 17 to discuss its proposed rights issue.
* Fishery firm Daya Guna Samudra might gain some attention on a report that Standard & Poor had assigned a BB-plus rating to its subsidiary's notes.
* Retailer Multipolar and supermarket Hero on renewed market speculation that Multipolar would buy a stake in Hero in the second half of this year.
* Small tourism firm Bayu Buana on market talk the firm would acquire some hotels belonging to an international group.
* Surabaya-based property firm Mas Murni Indonesia on continued talks that it would carry out a private placement at a price of 1,200 rupiah, brokers said.
